fluidDetails.name: Blood
fluidDetails.description: Primary forensic fluid. Contains DNA, proteins, ABO antigens, and hemoglobin markers. Most commonly analyzed in criminal investigations.

fluidDetails.name: Saliva
fluidDetails.description: Contains epithelial cells rich in DNA. Secretor status determines presence of ABO antigens. Found on cigarettes, cups, bite marks.

fluidDetails.name: Semen
fluidDetails.description: Critical in sexual assault cases. Contains spermatozoa and seminal plasma. Acid phosphatase testing used for preliminary identification.
fluidDetails.detection: AP test, PSA/P30, Christmas Tree stain

fluidDetails.name: Sweat
fluidDetails.description: Touch DNA source. Contains trace DNA from shed epithelial cells. Often found on handled objects, clothing, and grip surfaces.
fluidDetails.detection: Touch DNA extraction, skin cell analysis

fluidDetails.name: Urine
fluidDetails.description: Contains urea, creatinine, and trace DNA. Tamm-Horsfall protein is the primary confirmatory marker. Less DNA-rich than other fluids.

fluidDetails.name: Tears
fluidDetails.description: Contains lysozyme and lactoferrin proteins. Rare forensic specimen. Can yield DNA but typically low quantity and quality.
